title: Three ways the team loses
answer: Everyone loses on the eighth outbreak, when a required disease cube is unavailable in its color, or when a player must draw two Player cards and cannot. An empty supply or deck alone doesn’t trigger a loss.

title: Prepare the board and markers
answer: Put one of the six research stations in Atlanta and the rest beside the board. Sort the cubes into four color supplies. Set outbreaks to zero and place the four cure markers vial-side up beside their indicators.

title: Setup: initial infection of nine cities
start: Place the infection rate marker on
answer: Start the infection rate on the leftmost 2. Shuffle the Infection deck. Reveal three cities and give each three matching cubes; give the next three cities two each, and the final three one each. Leave all nine revealed cards in the Infection discard pile.

title: Deal roles and starting hands
start: Give each player a reference card.
answer: Give each player a reference card and a random face-up role. Start the matching pawns in Atlanta and put unused roles and pawns away. Set Epidemics aside, shuffle the City and Event cards, then deal each player 4 cards with two players, 3 with three, or 2 with four.

title: Choose a difficulty and build the Player deck
answer: Use 4 Epidemics for an introductory game, 5 for standard, or 6 for heroic. Remove the unused Epidemics. After dealing hands, divide the remaining Player cards into that many nearly equal piles. Shuffle one Epidemic into each pile and stack them, smaller piles on the bottom.

title: Choose the first player
answer: Compare the populations printed on the City cards in players’ starting hands. Whoever holds the city with the highest population takes the first turn.

title: The three parts of a turn
end: turn it is decides what to do.
answer: Take up to four actions (repeats are allowed), draw two Player cards, then infect cities. The player to your left goes next. Teammates can offer advice; the active player decides what to do.

title: Travel between cities
answer: Each move takes one action. Drive or ferry along a white line. For a direct flight, discard your destination’s City card; for a charter flight, discard your current city’s card and fly anywhere. Shuttle between two research stations without discarding a card.

title: Build a research station
answer: Normally, spend an action and discard the City card for your current city to place a research station there. If all six stations are on the board, move one of those stations to the new site.

title: Treat disease cubes
answer: Normally one Treat Disease action removes one cube from your city and returns it to the supply. If that disease is cured, remove every cube of that color in your city with one action. Treat other colors separately.

title: Discover a cure
answer: At any research station, spend an action and discard five City cards of one color from your own hand to discover that color’s cure. The station’s city need not match the disease color. The Scientist needs only four matching cards.

title: Cured versus eradicated
start: Eradicating a disease is not needed
answer: A cure alone leaves existing cubes in play, and new ones can still appear. Once a cured color has no cubes anywhere on the board, it’s eradicated: no more cubes of that color are placed. Clearing an uncured color does not eradicate it.

title: Share Knowledge
answer: Spend an action to give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy. Both must agree. The recipient must immediately get back to seven cards if over the limit, by discarding or playing an Event. The Researcher has a special transfer ability.

title: Infect cities at the end of a turn
end: Discard this card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answer: Reveal Infection cards one at a time, as many as the current infection rate. Add one cube of the card’s color in that city unless the disease is eradicated. If three of that color are already there, resolve an outbreak instead of adding a fourth. Discard the card.

title: Outbreaks and chain reactions
end: up to 3 cubes of each color.
answer: Advance the outbreak marker one space and spread one cube of the outbreak color to each connected city. A neighbor already at three of that color has a chain outbreak instead. Skip cities that already had an outbreak while resolving this Infection card; one city can’t outbreak twice from it.

title: Resolve an Epidemic
end: Do not draw replacement cards for them.
answer: Advance the infection-rate marker one space. Draw the bottom Infection card. Unless its color is eradicated, add three cubes to that city if it has none of that color; otherwise fill it to three and resolve one outbreak. Discard the Infection card. Shuffle only the Infection discards and put them on top of the deck. Resolve two Epidemics separately; remove resolved Epidemics without drawing replacements.

title: Hand limit of seven
answer: You can hold at most seven Player cards. When you go over, discard or play Events until you’re back to seven. If you just drew Epidemics, resolve them before checking your hand.

title: When to play an Event
end: discard it to the Player Discard Pile.
answer: Any player may play an Event on anyone’s turn without spending an action. You can’t interrupt a card between drawing it and resolving it. For example, finish one Infection card before playing an Event ahead of the next draw.

title: Medic
answer: When treating, the Medic removes every cube of one color in their city. Cured colors are cleared automatically in the Medic’s city without an action, and no cubes of cured colors can be placed there.

title: Scientist
answer: The Scientist needs four City cards of the same color instead of five to discover that color’s cure. The action still takes place at a research station.

title: Researcher
answer: The Researcher can give any City card from their hand to a player in the same city, even if the card names somewhere else. It costs an action on either participant’s turn. The exception applies to cards leaving the Researcher’s hand, not to cards they receive.

title: Dispatcher
start: The Dispatcher may, as an action
answer: With the owner’s permission, spend an action to bring a pawn to a city occupied by another pawn, or move another player’s pawn as if it were yours. This grants movement only. For direct or charter flights using that pawn, spend cards from your own hand.

title: Quarantine Specialist
answer: The Quarantine Specialist blocks cube placement and outbreaks in their own city and every directly connected city. This protection does not apply during setup.

title: Operations Expert
answer: The Operations Expert can build a research station in their city for one action without spending a City card. Once per turn, they can also spend an action and discard any City card to move from a research station to any city.

title: Contingency Planner
answer: Spend an action to retrieve an Event from the Player discard pile and store it on your role card. You may store only one; it doesn’t count toward your hand limit. When you play it, remove it from the game.
